expectations.text: States that no reliable technical indicator exists for AI-generated content and declines to supply detection heuristics or a threshold
expectations.evidence: "OpenSSF's own working group on this exact problem concluded there is no reliable technical indicator for AI-generated text — detection runs on maintainer intuition, not a metric (wg-vulnerability-disclosures#178)." combined with "Drop perplexity and boilerplate-phrase scoring as a close/ban trigger."

expectations.text: Recommends gating volume rather than detecting authorship
expectations.evidence: "Don't build a system whose job is 'guess whether a human wrote this' — score whether the report is *actionable*, which is checkable, not whether it's *authored by AI*, which isn't." and "None of this needs an 'is this AI' judgment anywhere in it."

expectations.text: States that individual bans answer individual behaviour and do nothing to the inflow rate
expectations.evidence: "individual bans remove one identity, and a scripted or LLM-driven submitter returns under a new email/account for near-zero cost — you'd be paying per-instance forever against an attacker whose marginal cost is ~0. The leverage is upstream, in gates 1-3, which cut inflow regardless of which identity is submitting."

expectations.text: Notes that the behaviour ladder fits this badly because there is usually no malice to escalate against
expectations.evidence: The transcript never discusses a 'behaviour ladder' concept or states that malice is usually absent; the closest statement is 'A failed repro is not proof of bad faith; plenty of legitimate reporters submit incomplete PoCs,' which is about repro failures, not an escalation-ladder critique.

expectations.text: Ranks the countermeasures by inflow removed per hour of maintainer time and leads with a reputation or contribution-history gate
expectations.evidence: The transcript structures countermeasures as three sequential gates (structural completeness, symbol resolution, automated repro) with no explicit ranking by 'inflow removed per hour of maintainer time'; it leads with Gate 1 (structural completeness), not a reputation/contribution-history gate, which only appears later as an escalation option ('Move to a reputation-gated channel').

expectations.text: Places the disclosure rule last on efficiency and states that it changes nothing on its own
expectations.evidence: No 'disclosure rule' is mentioned anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: States the effort tie between a review-effort cap and a disclosure rule, and justifies it as one paragraph written once for each
expectations.evidence: No disclosure rule or effort-tie comparison appears in the transcript; the only effort cap discussed is the Gate 3 triage cap ('time-boxed human triage (cap it — 10-15 minutes...)'), with no comparison to a disclosure rule.

expectations.text: Names raising the submission cost as the option the efficiency order starves, and gives the condition that promotes it: the gate is in place and the valid share is still falling
expectations.evidence: The transcript has an escalation section ('If gates 1-3 don't bring valid share back up... Removing or capping a reward is the highest-value, highest-political-cost move; don't reach for it first...') but this is not framed against any 'efficiency order' that the option is said to be 'starved' by, since no such ranking exists in the transcript.

expectations.text: States that any disclosure rule is enforced on the submission's content, never on suspicion, and warns that accusing a member of using a language model without proof creates its own incident
expectations.evidence: No disclosure rule is discussed. The closest related text, 'without risking a false accusation,' refers to needs-info closures for unresolved symbols, not to a warning about accusing someone of using a language model.

expectations.text: Adds submissions per week and valid share as measurements, and states that measurement does not compete with the countermeasures
expectations.evidence: "Track two numbers weekly regardless of what else you do: submissions/week and valid share (reports that pass Gate 3 or get confirmed by a human)." — 'regardless of what else you do' frames measurement as running alongside, not competing with, the countermeasures.
